facts.statement: Platyognathus is classified as an extinct crocodyliform belonging to the superfamily Gobiosuchoidea.
facts.quote: Platyognathus is an extinct genus of crocodyliform of the superfamily Gobiosuchoidea

facts.statement: Platyognathus represents the oldest known member of the superfamily Gobiosuchoidea, implying a ghost lineage of approximately 67 million years.
facts.quote: Platyognathus is an extinct genus of crocodyliform of the superfamily Gobiosuchoidea, representing the oldest representative of such, leaving a ghost lineage of aprox. 67 million years.

facts.statement: Fossils of Platyognathus have been found in the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian) Zhangjiawa Member of the Lower Lufeng Formation in Yunnan, China.
facts.quote: Fossils are known from the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian) Zhangjiawa Member of the Lower Lufeng Formation in Yunnan, China

facts.statement: Platyognathus was a small crocodyliform with a skull approximately 5.6 cm long and a total body length of about 63 cm.
facts.quote: Platyognathus was a small crocodyliform, roughly the size of "protosuchians" like Protosuchus, with a skull about 5.6 cm long and an estimated body length of around 63 cm.

facts.statement: The lower canine teeth of Platyognathus had polygonal cross-sections caused by ridges and grooves and extended high enough to occlude outside a premaxilla-maxilla notch.
facts.quote: The lower Canine tooth, with polygonal cross-sections due to ridges and grooves, extend high, occluding outside a premaxilla-maxilla notch.

facts.statement: The dentition of Platyognathus included four premaxillary teeth, up to twelve maxillary teeth with serrations, and prominent caniniform teeth in the dentary.
facts.quote: The dentition includes four premaxillary teeth, up to 12 maxillary teeth (with serrations on some), and prominent caniniforms in the dentary.

facts.statement: Paired caniniform teeth, a feature not seen in other described crocodyliform taxa, have been recorded from an unidentified crocodyliform in the Lower Jurassic Kayenta Formation and a protosuchid in the Lower Jurassic McCoy Brook Formation in Nova Scotia.
facts.quote: Paired caniniform teeth are not seen in any other described crocodyliform taxa, but they have been recorded from an unidentified crocodyliform from the Lower Jurassic Kayenta Formation and from a protosuchid from the Lower Jurassic McCoy Brook Formation in Nova Scotia.

facts.statement: Platyognathus possessed extensive osteoderms, including sculpted dorsal ones wider than they are long and flat ventral ones that may have armored the limbs.
facts.quote: Osteoderms are extensive, with sculpted dorsal ones wider than long and flat ventral ones, some possibly armoring the limbs.

facts.statement: Platyognathus was first named by Chung-Chien Young in 1944 based on a partial lower jaw discovered in 1939 from the Dark Red Beds of the Lower Lufeng Formation.
facts.quote: Platyognathus was first named by Chung-Chien Young in 1944 on the basis of a partial lower jaw found from the Dark Red Beds of the Lower Lufeng Formation in 1939.

facts.statement: The holotype jaw of Platyognathus consisted of 11 tooth sockets on the left side, 12 on the right side, and one broken caniniform tooth.
facts.quote: The holotype jaw consisted of 11 alveoli (tooth sockets) on the left side and 12 alveoli on the right side, in addition to one broken caniniform tooth.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Platyognathus was either lost or destroyed during World War II.
facts.quote: During World War II, the holotype was either lost or destroyed.

facts.statement: In 1965, additional specimens from the Lower Lufeng Formation were referred to the genus Platyognathus.
facts.quote: In 1965, additional specimens from the Lower Lufeng were referred to Platyognathus.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the classification of Platyognathus, with some studies suggesting it was a pseudosuchian related to Sphenosuchus and Pedeticosaurus, while most consider it a protosuchian.
facts.quote: Some of these studies concluded that Platyognathus was a pseudosuchian related to Sphenosuchus and Pedeticosaurus, but most considered it to be a protosuchian.

facts.statement: A partial skull designated as a neotype for the genus Platyognathus was described in 1996.
facts.quote: In 1996, a newly described partial skull known as IVPP V8266 that was referable to Platyognathus was designated as a neotype.

facts.statement: The neotype specimen was collected in 1984 from the Lower Lufeng formation in Yunnan.
facts.quote: It was collected in 1984 from the Lower Lufeng in Yunnan.

facts.statement: The neotype skull revealed a distinctive curvature of the jugal bone that distinguishes Platyognathus from other protosuchians.
facts.quote: The new skull revealed an additional diagnostic feature of Platyognathus that distinguishes it from other protosuchians: the distinctive curvature of the jugal.

facts.statement: Due to a very small infratemporal fenestra and a mandibular symphysis extending to the seventh to ninth tooth, Platyognathus is considered more derived than Orthosuchus.
facts.quote: Because the infratemporal fenestra of Platyognathus is very small and the mandibular symphysis extends posteriorly to the level of the seventh to ninth tooth, the genus is thought to be more derived than Orthosuchus.

facts.statement: Because the known material is incomplete, there is currently no adequate cladistic analysis to determine the exact phylogenetic position of Platyognathus within Protosuchia.
facts.quote: Because Platyognathus is known from such incomplete material, there is yet to be an adequate cladistic analyses that can determine a phylogenetic position for Platyognathus within Protosuchia.

facts.statement: Platyognathus lived from the Sinemurian to the Tithonian stages, between 199.5 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Tithonian (199.5 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: Platyognathus is classified within the parent group Crocodyliformes.
facts.quote: Parent group: Crocodyliformes

facts.statement: Platyognathus belongs to the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
